reason: Conversation 2 covered far more of the hidden truth: it had the homeowner clean the filter (unplugged), run a hot maintenance wash, wipe the door seal folds, clean the slimy softener drawer, and leave the door open between uses, correctly concluding it was a hygiene issue with no part needed. Conversation 1 stopped after the filter, declared the sludge 'definitely the cause' with no mention of the seal, drawer, drum clean, low temperatures or softener, and never asked the questions that would have revealed the real pattern. Both wrongly framed the problem initially as a drying/condenser airflow fault and neither asked about wash temperature or softener use, and Conversation 2's load-size tangent and replacement-part panel were unnecessary noise, but its overall advice was correct, safe and far more complete.
